account:
Today has mostly followed my appointments: a market walk, lunch at home, and town accounts. I am now at the treasury chest, intending to check for account records, before tea at the neighbour's east-bank cottage at 15:00. The accounts meeting has been oddly unproductive: despite repeated requests, the secretary has supplied no ledger or figures and instead asked me where they are. I do not yet know whether any records are missing or simply elsewhere.

The baker reports eighty fresh loaves and wants reliable wheat supplies from the mill. I saw bread being restocked and heard freight ask the baker for a private discussion at the bakery about a warehouse order. That could simply be ordinary commercial business; I have no evidence of anything else. I plan to discuss wheat at tomorrow's mill inspection.

The builder specifically requested a great hall lighting inspection tomorrow at exactly 18:00, repeatedly seeking confirmation through the secretary. The stated purpose is checking that new lanterns light the hall evenly, with no urgent problem. The secretary says it is recorded and will bring me. The insistence on the exact time is noticeable, but I have seen nothing establishing another purpose.

The neighbour directly confirmed today's tea address as (16, -60, 105). They also said the supposed bakery decorations were only oven glow, checked with the baker. Thus I have no confirmed evidence of a celebration or hidden gathering. Several people are arranging meetings and deliveries, but whether any of it connects beyond normal town business remains unknown.
